newsitem.title: USA: US Senate panel rejects bond simplification plan.
newsitem.headline: US Senate panel rejects bond simplification plan.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Finance Committee late Thursday narrowly defeated four proposed amendments to tax cut legislation designed to simplify the tax code for municipal bond issuers, a Senate aide said.
The aide to Sen. Bob Graham, who sponsored the proposals which lost on a 10-10 tie vote, said his boss may reoffer them when the full Senate takes up the tax package.
The overall tax cut bill won committee approval near midnight by an 18-2 vote.
"The senator is considering his options on offering the amendments on the floor or (adding) them to other legislation," the Graham aide said.

* Increased the small arbitrage rebate exemption from the current $5 million to $25 million for certain education facilities. Note that the overall tax bill approved last night still includes language pushed by Graham earlier this week to raise the current exemption to $10 million;
* Allowed banks to purchase up to $25 million in small issue education facility construction bonds annually, instead of the current $10 million limit;
* Provided a simplified three-year safe harbor for exemption from arbitrage rebate rules for financing certain facilities; and
* Created a category of exempt facility bonds for certain education facilities that would be subject to a separate cap on bond volume equal to $10 per capita annually.
Graham, D-Fla., decided not to press for a fifth amendment that would allow tax-exempt financed education facilities to receive accelerated depreciation, the aide said.
Micah Green, executive vice president of PSA The Bond Market Trade Association, said that even though Graham's package failed, last night's vote is "encouraging" for the muni market.
"A 10-10 vote is a very encouraging sign that the base of support for using bonds to meet public needs is on the rise," Green said in a telephone interview.

Green noted that Graham proposed raising the revenues needed to pay for his amendments by modifying HOPE scholarship credits. Green said the vote on bond simplification probably would have been higher if the scholarships were not used as an offset.
"Members of the committee who normally would support bond liberalization such as this voted no principally because of the revenue raiser," Green said.

Graham's aide noted that four Republicans voted for his boss' muni bond package, including Sens. John Chafee, R.I.; Alfonse D'Amato, N.Y.; Charles Grassley, R-Iowa; and Connie Mack, Fla. On the other hand, three Democrats opposed it, he said.
